Something moves out there — the thing with headlights for eyes, standing too still.

Kieran leans in, voice low. "Here's what we figured out about the creek went still, and your arm-hairs stood up. Get OUT of the water. When the crackling starts, step onto dry ground — the discharge cannot reach you there. On land it is just a long blind fish: slow, harmless, dinner. Never fight it standing in the creek."

No walls. No warning but the noise.

🚨 the thing with headlights for eyes, standing too still, a dog-shaped silence at the treeline, a drumbeat with no drummer, getting closer, something displaced a LOT of water, and it wasn't a log is at Haven's door. The village looks to you. Four ways to call: a RUNNER (slow, dangerous), a SIGNAL FIRE (fast, loud, everyone sees), the SYSTEM RELAY (if it can carry voices), or an ABILITY CRY (if your build has one). Each with honest costs.

📓 Journal: the thing with headlights for eyes, standing too still, a dog-shaped silence at the treeline, a drumbeat with no drummer, getting closer, something displaced a LOT of water, and it wasn't a log at the door, day 7.
One of them is coming for YOU — the thing with headlights for eyes, standing too still, inside the haven, eyes on your bedroll.
◈ NEURAL CREEP — the overlay isn't on the world anymore. It's under it. Behind your eyes, faintly, when you blink.
You don't know what that was. The thing with headlights for eyes, standing too still. Someone at the haven should hear about this.
💡 COUNTER LEARNED — Highbeam Deer: MOVE, don't stare. When it goes still, the beam is coming — MOVE, don't stare at the light. Anything beats standing there: the freeze means it is already aiming.
📓 Codex: Counter: MOVE, don't stare — When it goes still, the beam is coming — MOVE, don't stare at the light. Anything beats standing there: the freeze means it is already aiming.
The light touches the ground where you were standing. It has not found you yet.
The beam carves a bright arc across the ground, swinging after its target. It does not blink. It does not hurry.
The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Grace blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
